pr_title: Bluetooth: audio: Improve stream coupling for CIS as the unicast client
pr_body:
Allow  the streams to be paired when creating unicast group. This will
allow to reuse the same ISO for the paired streams.

Fixes: #51796
Signed-off-by: Mariusz Skamra <mariusz.skamra@codecoup.pl>

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Improve stream coupling for CIS as the unicast client
comments:
Regarding to "An Initiator should wait for all Sink ASEs to be used for the intended use case to transition to the Streaming state before sending audio data on any of the associated unicast Audio Streams. The waiting time is implementation specific.

This implies that in the above TWS scenario, CAP would actually expect us to either wait for the second device, or to tear down the existing group and recreate it with all streams once the second device has connected (which is possible with the current API)." 
Seems this would be complex. There second acceptor could be connected by initiator at anytime, could be when initiator just connected with first acceptor, and then initiator needs to teardown the CIG immediately which it just created.

> Seems this would be complex. There second acceptor could be connected by initiator at anytime, could be when initiator just connected with first acceptor, and then initiator needs to teardown the CIG immediately which it just created.

I agree. I think it is important to note that this is only a `should`, and it is allowed to either way. We might want to ask the GAWG about this, to see if the following really is the intention:

1. Connect Acceptor A
2. Start audio streams for Acceptor A
3. Wait
4. Connect Acceptor B
5. Stop audio streams for Acceptor A
6. Start audio streams for Acceptor A and Acceptor B

Another option is to make a `bt_audio_stream` object to be related 1:1 to CIS (Connected Isochronous **Stream**). ;) It would be straightforward to the user that is familiar with Core specification. We would not need to `pair` the streams as the `bt_audio_stream` would represent either unidirectional or bidirectional CIS.
Currently stream is related 1:1 to endpoint instead.

> Another option is to make a `bt_audio_stream` object to be related 1:1 to CIS (Connected Isochronous **Stream**). ;) It would be straightforward to the user that is familiar with Core specification. We would not need to `pair` the streams as the `bt_audio_stream` would represent either unidirectional or bidirectional CIS. Currently stream is related 1:1 to endpoint instead.

Right. The current implementation of the `bt_audio_stream` follows the definition of an Audio Stream from BAP: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2520413/201678124-261b9be1-e115-4793-af84-0bb8d94f752c.png)


If we make it bidirectional, we lose the relationship with the BAP spec, but also make it harder to perform any of the ASE control point operations, as those are for specific ASEs, and not CIS. 

I am not objecting to making `bt_audio_stream` bidirectional, but I think it would require significant changes to the implementation.

@MariuszSkamra Somewhat related: After https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/51513/commits/f958b3b2bb210d0fc9c5dfdd734b29de34753ca6 was merged, the `stream->ep` is now required before a stream can be added to a unicast group. Since `stream->ep` is not set until after it has been configured, this also means that a device can no longer create a unicast group with streams, before the streams have been Codec Configured. The reasoning is that `unicast_group_add_stream` now uses the `ep` to get the direction, as well as storing the allocated `audio_iso` in `ep` only.

review_comments: Not necessarily, as user might not pair the streams.
True, but it matches the name of the parameter struct `bt_audio_unicast_group_stream_pair_param` better :)

Keep in mind that until `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_CENTRAL_ISO` gets enabled, creating the group here doesn't do anything.
